subject: Harborlane: AZ degradation and request for priority cross-region evacuation (authorization request)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborlane.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Li <ava.li@harborlane.com>, Harborlane SRE <support@harborlane.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: P1: Elevated latency and 5xx rates in us-west-2 — requesting immediate cross-region evacuation

Jasmine / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xxs and tail latency on our production tenant around 07:50 PDT. Error rate for /api/generate has jumped from ~0.2% to 6.8%, and p99 latency climbed from ~350ms to ~2.4s. This is impacting live checkout and personalization for Harborlane customers.

We believe the problem is concentrated in us-west-2 (usw2-a/b) — full request traces attached (network-trace-20270627.pcap) and service logs (svc-logs-hrb-27Jun.jsonl). Our SRE is seeing KV cache saturation and a lot of retry storms from long-running requests. Can Redwood trigger a regional evacuation / cross-region steer (us-east-2) while you investigate? We need an authorization from Redwood to proceed with any routing changes on your side.

We also need executive visibility — this is P1 for us. Please advise next steps and expected customer impact window.

—Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering | Harborlane
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborlane.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: P1: Elevated latency and 5xx rates in us-west-2 — requesting immediate cross-region evacuation

Tom — thanks for the quick alert and the artifacts. We see matching telemetry on our side (spike in request QPS + KV cache pressure). I’m standing up a bridge now and looping in SRE and engineering.

Immediate plan (proposal):
- Short-term: execute a controlled canary cross-region steer to us-east-2 for 20% of traffic for 30 minutes (to reduce pressure and confirm behavior).
- Mid-term: if canary stabilizes, roll to 100% with staged drains across affected AZs.
- Technical notes: this will change request egress region and can increase token costs and latency for a small subset of users; expect a transient 99.5% window during reroute.

We need explicit approval from Harborlane for the reroute and confirmation you accept a short window of degraded tail latency during cutover. Please reply with OK to proceed.

I’ve attached the playbook link and will post the bridge details in the next update. Prioritizing this for exec attention as requested.

—Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: P1: Elevated latency and 5xx rates in us-west-2 — technical assessment

Team — quick technical summary from SRE after ingesting Tom's artifacts:
- Root symptom: KV cache write amplification and GC pressure on us-west-2 KVC nodes after a sudden increase in long-sequence chat traffic from a third-party integration. Cache eviction thrashing led to increased backend calls and retry amplification.
- Autoscaling: the cluster attempted to scale but was delayed by cold-start times on a subset of instances and an internal queue backlog.
- Immediate mitigation: recommend an active egress steer to us-east-2 with the following steps:
  1) Toggle routing policy for Harborlane tenant to prefer us-east-2 (canary 20% -> observe 30 min).
  2) Increase per-tenant token quota temporarily to limit client retries (rate-limit smoothing).
  3) Warm KVC nodes in target region with synthetic prefixes to reduce cold starts.
- Risk: small fraction of sessions may see session-affinity breaks; we should surface guidance to Harborlane about short-lived token mismatch and a recommended client retry-backoff.

I’ve uploaded svc-logs-hrb-27Jun.jsonl and a condensed trace to the bridge. Ready to execute once we have customer OK and executive greenlight for priority capacity in us-east-2.

—Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborlane.com>, Ava Li <ava.li@harborlane.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Authorization request — priority capacity & commercial remediation

Quick commercial note — Harborlane is asking for executive visibility and is already flagging potential customer impact. I recommend we approve priority capacity in us-east-2 for the next 48 hours and offer a billing remediation (one-off credit) while we perform a full RCA.

Priyom — can you authorize a temporary override for Harborlane (priority allocation + waive overage for this incident window)? We should also prepare a one-page exec summary for Harborlane’s CTO and our Head of Sales.

Tom / Ava — appreciate the quick collaboration. If you approve, we’ll proceed with the canary steer immediately and send a short customer-facing note explaining the expected behavior and timeline.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@harborlane.com>, Ava Li <ava.li@harborlane.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization and execution confirmation — canary steer complete

All — status update from the bridge: canary steer (20% -> us-east-2) executed at 14:12 PDT and we observed the following within 18 minutes:
- us-west-2 5xx rate reduced from 6.8% to 1.1% over the canary window.
- overall p99 latency across affected endpoints dropped to ~420ms in the canary population.
- No major session-affinity break reports from Harborlane's telemetry during the canary.

We have started a staged roll to 100% with rolling drains across affected AZs — this is ongoing and expected to complete in next 60 minutes. I’ve attached a short handoff slide with timestamps (handoff_slide.pdf) and opened JIRA INF-8721 for the RCA.

Next steps:
- Formal RCA scheduled for 48 hours out; pre-RCA action items assigned in INF-8721.
- Vanessa: please prepare the credit proposal and exec note by EOD.
- Tom / Ava: please confirm when you have internal OK for full cutover to finish the roll.

Thanks team for the rapid turnaround. We’ll circulate the post-incident timeline and mitigation items after the RCA.

—Markus Klein
Director, Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
